Prevention: Do not use planting materials from infested plants for propagation.
Space or prune trees to ensure their canopies do not touch, to reduce the spread of mealybugs between trees.
Carry them away and destroy by burning.
Destroy ant colonies as they transport mealybugs.
Apply bands of sticky or alkathene sheets or a band of insecticide on arms or on main stem to prevent movement.
Remove host plants in and around the field such as tomato, hibiscus, beans, or establish your paw paw farm away from alternate hosts like guavas, mangoes and mulberry.
Conserve natural enemies of the papaya mealybug such as ladybird beetles, lacewings and hoverflies, by growing flowers and herbs such as cilantro, dill, fennel, caraway and yarrow.
Apeflies ( Spalgis lemolea ), a predator of aphids, by not applying broad spectrum insecticides.
Completely remove and bury or burn infested papaya residues.
Monitoring: Look for alternative host plants around your field such as hibiscus, avocado, citrus, cotton, tomato, eggplant, peppers, beans, peas, sweetpotato and mango.
Monitor and scout weekly to detect the early presence of mealybugs.
Look for clusters of cotton-like masses.
Look for mealybugs on fruit, leaves and stem as they appear covered with white wax.
A mealy is 2.0-3.5 mm long, soft- bodied, oval and flat; on maturation, she secretes sticky, elastic, white wax to form a protective sac for her yellow eggs.
Monitor damage symptoms such as chlorosis, plant stunting, leaf deformation, early leaf and fruit drop, a heavy build-up of honeydew.
If populations are high, as indicated by sooty mould, then consider control by spraying pesticides.
Action is too late when many pawpaw fruits are covered with wax and sooty mould.
When more than 10-20 mealybugs are seen per larger papaya, or 5-10 per small papaya, consider action.
Direct Control: Spray botanical insecticides every 7 days if threshold is reached; such as neem oil (1 to 2%), NSKE (5%), or
Soap (25g/litre of water, but check label).
Mix 2 teaspoons of mild liquid dish detergent in 4L of water.
Rinse the plant with fresh water after 2-3 hours, to avoid plant injury.
Spray the plant every 4-7 days if threshold is reached.
Use sticky bands on the trunk or branches to control ants and enhance the effectiveness of natural enemies.
Spray mineral oil to suffocate the mealybugs.
Malathion based products as per product label.
Restrictions: Insecticides are only used to control heavy infestations.

Dimethoate based products as per label.
